Build DEG sets and structured gene membership from differential expression results

rna_sets.Rd

Constructs structured gene sets from differential expression results stored in the active rna_project. This function formalizes DEGs as explicit sets, enabling downstream analyses such as overlaps, enrichment, and custom visualization.

Optionally, a summary plot of up- and down-regulated genes can be generated.

Usage

rna_sets(
  project,
  padj_cutoff = 0.05,
  log2fc_cutoff = 0.5,
  direction = c("both", "up", "down"),
  colors = NULL,
  plot = FALSE,
  save = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

project

rna_project object created by rna_project().

padj_cutoff

Numeric. Adjusted p-value threshold used to define significance (default: 0.05).

log2fc_cutoff

Numeric. Log2 fold-change threshold for directional classification (default: 0.5).

direction

Character. One of "both", "up", or "down". Determines which genes are flagged as DEGs in the main output (default: "both").

colors

Character. Optional bars colors.

plot

Logical. If TRUE, displays a barplot summarizing DEG counts per group (default: FALSE).

save

Logical. Whether to store results in the active rna_project (default: TRUE).

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, prints a summary to the console (default: TRUE).

Value

An object of class "rna_sets" containing:

deg

Logical vector indicating DEG membership after applying direction.

deg_all

Logical vector indicating all DEGs (independent of direction).

up

Logical vector for genes upregulated in the test group.

down

Logical vector for genes upregulated in the reference group.

one_hot

Data frame encoding gene membership across groups (one-hot format).

params

List of parameters and thresholds used to define sets.

Details

This function transforms differential expression results into explicit gene sets based on statistical significance and effect size thresholds.

DEG definition Genes are considered differentially expressed if:

  • padj < padj_cutoff

  • absolute log2 fold-change exceeds log2fc_cutoff

Directional classification

  • Upregulated genes: log2FC > log2fc_cutoff

  • Downregulated genes: log2FC < -log2fc_cutoff

Set representation The output includes multiple complementary representations:

  • Binary DEG membership (deg, deg_all)

  • Directional sets (up, down)

  • One-hot encoded matrix (one_hot) for set operations

This structure allows flexible downstream use, including intersections, enrichment analysis, and visualization.

Interpretation guide

  • The number of DEGs depends strongly on both padj_cutoff and log2fc_cutoff

  • Increasing the fold-change threshold yields more conservative, high-effect genes

  • Directional filtering is useful for asymmetric biological interpretations

The distinction between "up" and "down" depends on the contrast definition used in the original comparison.

Pipeline context

This function is typically used after rna_compare() to formalize DEG sets. The resulting object is designed to be used with downstream tools such as:

  • visualization (e.g., heatmaps, Venn diagrams)

  • enrichment analysis

  • custom set operations

It represents a key step in separating statistical testing from biological interpretation.

Important considerations

Threshold sensitivity DEG sets can vary substantially depending on cutoff choices. Always inspect results across multiple thresholds when possible.

Directionality depends on contrast The meaning of "up" and "down" is tied to the test vs reference groups defined in the original comparison.

Gene universe consistency Only genes present in both the expression matrix and comparison results are retained.

Side effects

If save = TRUE, results are stored in the rna_project under the analyses$rna_sets slot.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Build DEG sets from last comparison
rna_sets(project = my_project)

# More stringent thresholds
rna_sets(my_project,
         padj_cutoff = 0.01,
         log2fc_cutoff = 1
)

# Only upregulated genes
rna_sets(my_project,
         direction = "up")

# Plot DEG summary
rna_sets(my_project,
         plot = TRUE)

} # }
